loop_long_horizon_assessments.scope: Incremental relative-volume activity prediction is tested against a state model on identical origins. It does not establish causal liquidity costs.
loop_long_horizon_assessments.result: Activity worsens all 11 two-year same-origin state-model comparisons in both cleaning variants. It improves 8/11 five-year pragmatic comparisons, based on very few nonoverlapping spans; no causal liquidity verdict.

loop_lh2_evidence.finding: Original OLS two-year activity loss reproduced; fixed ridge activity helps 4/11 pragmatic, 5/11 strict comparisons. Specification dependence, no causal liquidity verdict.

loop_lh3_evidence.finding: Rolling OLS activity improves 1/11 two-year matched state comparisons; ridge improves 4/11 pragmatic and 5/11 strict. Original expanding OLS negative activity result preserved, no causal liquidity verdict.

loop_lh4_evidence.finding: Analyst flags News negative combined-spread coefficient as estimand-dependent tension with a naive universal liquidity story, not a causal result or established literature contradiction.

research_tracks.title: Public share supply and sustained trading capacity
research_tracks.question: Do years of relative supply and trading capacity explain persistent discount changes?
research_tracks.data: Quarterly class share counts, treasury/strategic holdings, executed actions, documented public float, and monthly trading costs/capacity.
research_tracks.test: Reconstruct supply and cost histories jointly; distinguish scarcity/support from deteriorating ability to trade and management responding to the gap.

research_tracks.title: Durable investor base, institutional demand and access
research_tracks.question: Who holds each class over years, and do changes in that investor base persistently reprice the classes?
research_tracks.data: Class-level quarterly/annual foreign and institutional holdings, holder concentration, retail participation, index/mandate histories and dated eligibility rules.
research_tracks.test: Separate ownership stocks from trading flows; compare durable class-relative ownership/access changes with discount regimes and comparable peers.

research_tracks.title: Control, minority rights and governance regimes
research_tracks.question: Does a sustained change in control or shareholder protection alter what common votes are worth?
research_tracks.data: Dated controller/affiliate blocks, independent blocks, agreements, succession/control events and effective legal/charter rules.
research_tracks.test: Distinguish lower unequal-treatment risk from more effective minority votes; test the two potentially opposing channels with actual ownership states.

research_tracks.title: Multi-year payout policy, cash rights and income investors
research_tracks.question: Do credible sustained cash-return policies change relative demand and the holding outcome of the two classes?
research_tracks.data: Dated policy commitments and changes, actual class cash payments, earnings/free cash flow, payout coverage and investor composition.
research_tracks.test: Compare policy eras and delivery over quarters/years; separate cash received from terminal discount and remove mechanical yield/price-ratio explanations.

research_tracks.title: Class structure, investor access and market integration
research_tracks.question: What verified structural change could permanently reduce segmentation or equalize class rights?
research_tracks.data: Historical class terms, conversion/unification proposals or implementation if any, receipt ratios/venues, access and ownership restrictions.
research_tracks.test: Audit a credible legal/economic convergence route before assigning it value; distinguish an actual change from a hypothetical scenario.

research_tracks.title: Cross-cutting constraints that allow a gap to last
research_tracks.question: Why can investors not cheaply maintain a position that closes the gap over years?
research_tracks.data: Lending/borrow availability and fees, applicable short-sale rules, funding conditions, holding costs and the existence or absence of a terminal event.
research_tracks.test: Evaluate persistence and the cost/risk of corrective positions alongside each leading mechanism; a short-sale ban alone is not a measured borrowing cost.

research_tracks.title: Company and economic cycles through a class-specific channel
research_tracks.question: Do multi-year company or macro cycles alter class demand, payout credibility or trading capacity differently?
research_tracks.data: Quarterly cash generation/capital spending, industry state, rates/FX, and observed class-specific transmission variables.
research_tracks.test: Require a differential-class channel; compare complete economic cycles and peers rather than re-labeling US style returns as Samsung fundamentals.

research_tracks.title: Measurement and legal foundations
research_tracks.question: Are the long-run price ratios, class rights and cash outcomes comparable?
research_tracks.data: Class identifiers, historical units/actions, independent calendar, entitlements and publication dates.
research_tracks.test: Validate monthly/quarterly aggregation and historical rights; use daily timing or ex-date tests only to resolve a material long-run ambiguity.

core_pair_extension.status: price baselines complete; Korean NAV regressions pending
core_pair_extension.scope: Retrospective B00 price-gap measurement for SK Square/SK Hynix, Samsung Fire/Samsung Electronics common, and TSMC local/ADR; no NAV, causal, forecasting, or trading inference.

evidence.sk_square_sk_hynix: HAC20 lag-gap coefficient -0.011528, p=0.00844, n=1149, adjusted R2=0.00561; normalized price ratio only.
evidence.samsung_fire_samsung_electronics: HAC20 lag-gap coefficient -0.001484, p=0.1299, n=5203, adjusted R2=0.000605; normalized price ratio only.
evidence.tsmc_local_adr: HAC20 lag-gap coefficient -0.069053, p=4.15e-20, n=4737, adjusted R2=0.03418; five shares per ADS and retrospective same-date noon-New-York FX.
evidence.adr_handoff: Five overlapping September 2026 closes matched exactly; CRSP through September 30 and Compustat North America October 1-November 6 with source tags and CRSP-only fields missing.
evidence.nav_gate: Individual Korean ownership observations do not form dated histories; annual/quarterly vendor dates are not verified public-release clocks. Keep Korean NAV branches untested.

hypothesis_implications: B00-like adjustment is an observed in-sample association for SK Square and TSMC but has low explanatory power and is not validated out of sample.
Samsung Fire's full-window adjustment coefficient is not distinguishable from zero at conventional levels.
The TSMC result is consistent with short-run cross-market adjustment but does not distinguish non-synchronous closes, FX timing, liquidity, access, or arbitrage constraints.
No Korean ownership, operating-business, or balance-sheet mechanism changes status from these price-only regressions.

questions.S06_L01: Supply levels mark regimes, but changes are null and stable-count-era discount variation rejects supply-only sufficiency; activity proxy also weak.
questions.M04_B03: Observed correction after widening is primarily preferred catch-up; common reversal contributes at five sessions only in the full sample.
questions.S01_S02_S03_P01: Recent programs are near-proportional and event paths mixed; no causal preferred-support result.
questions.TSMC_X02_X03_M04: Both later US ADR and next Taiwan local prices move toward parity; spread sensitivity preserves signs.

loop_exception_generalization.scope: Seven US share-class/preferred pairs, six holdco/heldco US proxy relationships, and cross-pair comparisons available from the LOOP Exceptions workbook; no NAV, causal, or fully costed trading inference.

questions.B02_B03_generalization: Five of seven share pairs have negative conventional-significance B00 coefficients, but only Berkshire and Liberty beat zero-change persistence in expanding forecasts; every pair beats the aggressive rolling-median forecast.
questions.M04_leg_adjustment: All seven pairs have negative average 1/5/20-session relative movement after a one-point widening; the right/relatively cheaper leg generally outperforms, with sparse events for Alphabet, Fox, and Liberty.
questions.L01_liquidity: Spread and turnover relationships are heterogeneous: positive spread association for Alphabet, Berkshire, and Petrobras, negative for News, weak for Fox/Liberty, and unavailable for Volkswagen.
questions.holdco_pass_through: Heldco betas range from 0.25 to about 1.00; only Liberty/Charter and SoftBank/Arm show conventional downside asymmetry. These are exposure regressions, not NAV discounts.
questions.common_factor: PC1 explains 16.22% of seven US differential changes and exact-calendar core-pair correlations are mostly small; no dominant global gap factor is supported.
questions.application: Quoted-spread diagnostics are positive for six estimable pairs, but missing borrow, dividends, taxes, locates, impact, and conversion costs prevent portfolio-performance claims.
questions.prosus_tencent_gap: Local-security B01-B04 gap sensitivity has n=1611 and adjusted R2 of 0.48%-0.71%; B03 lag-gap p=0.018 but q=0.634, B04 lag-gap p=0.071, and activity p=0.650. Weak descriptive adjustment only.

tree_implications: B02 is heterogeneous across pairs rather than universally rejected or supported; Berkshire is strongest, Liberty modest, and five fail persistence.
B03 gains broad descriptive correction evidence but remains noncausal and incompletely costed.
L01 remains pair-specific and unresolved globally.
Holdco and NAV mechanisms remain blocked wherever dated holdings, liabilities, taxes, and share counts are absent.
